record.original_question: Let S(t) = (1/pi) arg zeta(1/2 + it). Carneiro, Chandee, and Milinovich proved, under the Riemann Hypothesis, that |S(t)| <= (C0 + o(1)) log t / log log t with C0 = 1/4. Reduce the constant C0 in this estimate.

evidence.quote: Let S(t) = π1 arg ζ(1/2 + it). Carneiro, Chandee, and Milinovich [12] proved that the Riemann hypothesis implies |S(t)| <= (C0 + o(1)) · log t / log log t with C0 = 1/4. Reduce the value of C0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\zeta$ denote the Riemann zeta-function, and for real $t$ that is not the ordinate of a zero of $\zeta$, define
$$ S(t) =  rac{1}{\pi}\,\arg\zeta\!\left(	frac12 + itight), $$
where the argument is obtained by continuous variation along the horizontal segment from $2$ to $2+it$ and then along the vertical segment from $2+it$ to $	frac12+it$, starting with the value $0$ at $s=2$. (At ordinates of zeros, $S(t)$ is defined as the average of its left and right limits.)

Assume the Riemann Hypothesis: all nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ lie on the critical line $\Re s = 	frac12$. Under this assumption, it is known that
$$ |S(t)| \;\le\;  igl(C_0 + o(1) igr)\, rac{\log t}{\log\log t} \qquad (t	o\infty), $$
with the admissible value $C_0 = 	frac14$.

Problem: Determine an admissible constant $C_0 < 	frac14$ for which the above inequality continues to hold (under the Riemann Hypothesis), i.e.\ improve the constant $	frac14$ in this asymptotic bound for $|S(t)|$.
artifact.status_search_result: The bound |S(t)| ≤ (1/4 + o(1)) log t / log log t under RH due to Carneiro–Chandee–Milinovich is still the sharpest known. The order of magnitude has not been improved since Littlewood (1924), and the implicit constant 1/4 remains the best published value; no improvement of the leading constant appears to have been recorded as of 2026. The problem of reducing C_0 below 1/4 thus appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Bounding S(t) and S1(t) on the Riemann hypothesis
status_evidence.snippet: The best bounds for S(t) and S1(t) under RH are currently due to Carneiro, Chandee and Milinovich, giving the sharpest known bound for S(t).
status_evidence.claim: C0 = 1/4 is the current sharpest constant in the bound for |S(t)| under RH.

status_evidence.title: A survey on Beurling–Selberg majorants and some of its applications
status_evidence.snippet: Efforts have been concentrated on optimizing the values of the implicit constants in Littlewood's O(log t / (log log t)^{n+1}) bound, since the order of magnitude has not been improved.
status_evidence.claim: Improvements to the implicit constant in the S(t) bound is an active area, but the constant 1/4 still stands.
